objective: Exploratory characterization under a frozen contract of ticket B's 1,120 native paths: whether any stays native when its second middle ring is made uniform with one of the eight linear rules (is hybridness necessary), whether nativeness survives transport (one more cell in the second middle ring, or in an end ring), which ring-C cells' first rows stay in the last contact's eventual support and through which side the first ring's influence arrives, and the canonical check of the smallest (generic enumerator on the last contact's two-time law, knotlab check on its eventual parity).
status: Supported 2026-11-08 (exploratory): every one of the 1,120 native paths needs its hybrid ring (no uniform linear ring keeps it native); the last contact's support keeps two or three of the hybrid ring's own cells; one more cell keeps some variant native for 704 (ring C), 928 (ring D) and 0 (ring A) of them; the smallest's knot through c3(T) meets all four rings at lags 5 to 10, confirmed by knotlab.
title: What makes a hybrid middle ring work
